reviews.review:
The game features truly epic battles and a great sense of progression throughout the campaign on NORMAL difficulty. There is a solid variety of enemies, and weapon types function fundamentally differently even within the same category. You have vehicles and four distinct classes that feel genuinely unique, plus co-op support. There are plenty of missions, and they are quite diverse. It is easily one of the best horde-shooters I’ve ever played. However, not everything is executed perfectly.

It’s a shame that such a great concept is wrapped in outdated graphics with clunky animations, and many enemies often get stuck between buildings or rocks.

I’m also disappointed that the entire loot and progression system breaks down when moving to higher difficulty levels. On Hard, the game only starts giving you new, better weapons starting from mission 50. On the highest difficulty, new gear only drops from mission 25 onwards, even though the enemies become exponentially stronger right from the start. I don’t understand the logic here; if you're tackling tougher campaign levels, it would be logical to continue player progression by providing upgraded weapon models immediately, starting from the first missions.

Furthermore, the difficulty isn't sufficiently balanced by the weapons you receive. Enemies turn into damage sponges, gaining several times more health, while new weapons only provide a 1.5x–2x damage boost (and almost all new weapons are just slightly improved versions of the old ones). By the time I reached Hardest difficulty, I lost my grip on the overall game design. Regular ants deal 500 damage in close combat, and they get close often because you can't control the whole swarm due to insufficient DPS. As a result, the ants scatter and flank you from behind. For example, despite having nearly 2,000 HP, I failed a mission because two elite ants attacked me at close range simultaneously. A 10-minute mission ended in defeat just because I missed two attacks from elite ants. Perhaps this difficulty requires more health, but how much grinding does that take? One full campaign run nets you about +500 HP. It feels like you need at least 10,000 HP to feel somewhat comfortable on Hardest. With my 2,000 HP, does that mean I need to replay the campaign 16 more times before stepping up? Hundreds of hours of grinding? Or do I have to farm a single mission on Easy to get +5 HP per minute, which translates to 27 hours of farming the same map? It all feels excessively padded.

That said, the way difficulty scales is conceptually well-done in many aspects. Enemies don't just become tankier and hit harder—they get faster, missions feature new events, and enemies fire more projectiles, making them more accurate. The difficulty is genuinely well-thought-out in terms of changing enemy mechanics.

However, the loot system is also flawed because many weapons feel more like a joke than something viable for combat. The same goes for receiving weapons that are impossible to use solo because they require support from another class. Overall, while playing the solo campaign, I began to notice that many levels are designed strictly for co-op, where players can cover different lanes and classes can offset each other's weaknesses. When playing alone, the AI soldiers don't come close to filling the role of human players, turning some missions into a chaotic mess that is barely beatable on high difficulties.

You know, a few flaws here and there couldn't hurt; some of the weapons arsenal don't usually mean much but they can be fun for what they can offer; or something I'd wish there's a Self Propelled AA over here but that's on EDF 6, using Helicopters brings such dread; yet after 60+ hours... this game is definitely worth it for me; matter of fact. EDF Franchise itself is always an amazing one despite the odds. 

♫ Now pick up our weapons, off we go. ♫
♫ Firing at the flying saucers, shooting down our foe. ♫
♫ We shall not allow these aliens, to rule we ♥♥♥♥ sapiens.♫
